governingInquiry: How does the open loyalty system improve the amount, relevance, reliability, accessibility, usefulness and appropriate speed with which loyalty opportunities become realized member value across its different relationship pathways?

classificationModel.rule: Group convergence and hypotheses never become evidence-supported solely through approval.

sources.title: Interactive Loyalty Systems Map — Analytical Architecture Output Contract

boundary.purpose: Analyze how loyalty opportunities become realized member value across an open loyalty, banking and partner ecosystem.
premises: Member-Only participants must be able to realize credible standalone value.
Conversion is optional, relevant and need-led.
Member-Client status does not prove realized or incremental value.
Partner and organizational outcomes remain distinct from member realized value.

nodes.label: Member-only
nodes.subtitle: Program relationship
nodes.definition: A person who belongs to the loyalty program but does not currently hold a banking relationship with the client.
nodes.roleInSystem: This population sustains the open program ecosystem through earning, redemption and partner participation. It is also the largest immediate population from which relevant banking relationships might be created.
nodes.whyItMatters: The program was designed to serve people beyond the bank. Preserving credible standalone value is therefore necessary both for member trust and for the client’s future relationship opportunity.
nodes.known: Member-only participants can receive program and partner value without becoming clients. Research shows that members judge programs by usable value, flexibility and reliable delivery—not ownership alone.
nodes.provisional: The active size of this population, the data that may be used for banking decisioning, and the proportion with a relevant banking need remain unconfirmed.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Use permissioned member context to recognize genuine financial needs and present bank-connected value without making conversion a condition for receiving worthwhile program value.

claims.text: Member-only participants can receive program and partner value without becoming clients. Research shows that members judge programs by usable value, flexibility and reliable delivery—not ownership alone.
The active size of this population, the data that may be used for banking decisioning, and the proportion with a relevant banking need remain unconfirmed.

nodes.label: Member-client
nodes.subtitle: Program + banking relationship
nodes.definition: A person who simultaneously participates in the loyalty program and holds a banking relationship with the client.
nodes.roleInSystem: This is the strategic intersection where program value, banking value and partner value can potentially be coordinated across one relationship.
nodes.whyItMatters: The client expects the intersection to support deeper engagement and greater relationship value. Bank-linked products already demonstrate that members can receive additional earning routes and benefits.
nodes.known: Member-clients may have access to a higher potential value ceiling through connected products, enhanced earning and integrated channels.
nodes.provisional: Holding both relationships does not prove engagement, affinity or incremental value. The combined value must still be relevant, used, fulfilled and realized.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Coordinate program, banking and partner value so the intersection produces recognizably better outcomes rather than simply a larger number of linked accounts.

claims.text: Member-clients may have access to a higher potential value ceiling through connected products, enhanced earning and integrated channels.
Holding both relationships does not prove engagement, affinity or incremental value. The combined value must still be relevant, used, fulfilled and realized.

nodes.label: Client-only
nodes.subtitle: Banking relationship
nodes.definition: A banking client who does not currently participate in this loyalty program.
nodes.roleInSystem: This population can enter the intersection through relevant program enrolment. Existing transactions and participation in other reward products may indicate potential fit.
nodes.whyItMatters: The client already has channels, products and permissioned banking context that may help explain where program participation could add value.
nodes.known: A client may already use cashback, points or co-branded products outside this program. Those behaviours show broader loyalty engagement, but not engagement with this specific program.
nodes.provisional: Transaction activity is only a relevance signal. It does not prove interest, consent, product suitability or willingness to manage another loyalty relationship.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Identify where program participation complements an existing client need, then reduce the friction required to enrol, earn and realize the first meaningful benefit.

claims.text: A client may already use cashback, points or co-branded products outside this program. Those behaviours show broader loyalty engagement, but not engagement with this specific program.
Transaction activity is only a relevance signal. It does not prove interest, consent, product suitability or willingness to manage another loyalty relationship.

nodes.label: Partner ecosystem
nodes.subtitle: Merchants • experiences • business relationships
nodes.definition: Merchants and business partners that contribute products, services, offers, access or experiences to the loyalty ecosystem.
nodes.roleInSystem: Partners expand what members can earn, access and redeem while connecting the program to everyday and aspirational needs.
nodes.whyItMatters: Partner quality, frequency and relevance determine practical value more than the nominal number of brands in the ecosystem.
nodes.known: Partners can receive sales, attention, repeat purchasing and potential share-of-wallet gains. They may also receive permissioned or aggregated performance insight.
nodes.provisional: The incrementality of partner sales, actual data-sharing arrangements, offer funding and partner economics are not yet established.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Create a reciprocal value exchange in which relevant partner contributions strengthen engagement and demonstrated partner returns encourage continued participation.

claims.text: Partners can receive sales, attention, repeat purchasing and potential share-of-wallet gains. They may also receive permissioned or aggregated performance insight.
The incrementality of partner sales, actual data-sharing arrangements, offer funding and partner economics are not yet established.

nodes.label: Realized value
nodes.subtitle: The main variable
nodes.definition: The value members actually obtain and can use — the amount of worthwhile value that makes it all the way through to them. This is the system's main variable: the thing the whole map is organised around and the measure the team agreed to be judged on.
nodes.roleInSystem: This is the system main variable. It connects relevance, qualification, posting, access, use, fulfilment and perceived worth without treating activity alone as success.
nodes.whyItMatters: The system exists to improve the amount, relevance, reliability, accessibility, usefulness and appropriate speed with which loyalty opportunities become realized member value across its relationship pathways.
nodes.known: The analytical model distinguishes Opportunity, Potential, Earned, Available and Realized. Empirical transition rates and drop-offs remain unknown.
nodes.provisional: The largest realization gaps, causal drivers, population differences and incremental outcomes remain unresolved.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Improve value progression across multiple dimensions while preserving credible standalone Member-Only value and avoiding speed-only optimization.

claims.text: Realized value is the main variable and organizing construct.
Actual transition rates, delays and population-level gaps are not yet established.

nodes.label: Meaningful engagement
nodes.subtitle: Frequency • breadth • continuity • completion • progression
nodes.definition: A sustained, multidimensional pattern of participation over time, described through frequency, breadth, continuity, completion and progression.
nodes.roleInSystem: Meaningful Engagement may follow repeated worthwhile value realization and provides participation and outcome signals back into the system. It is not the main variable.
nodes.whyItMatters: Sustained participation may indicate that outcomes are worthwhile, but activity, earning, redemption or linked relationships do not by themselves prove realized value.
nodes.known: Participation is observable through actions such as earning, redeeming, using benefits or adopting relevant products. Activation initiates or renews that participation; repeated participation develops into engagement.
nodes.provisional: Engagement does not automatically cause conversion, affinity or revenue. Its effect depends on relevance, realized value, trust, suitability and reliable delivery.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Learn whether and under what conditions repeated worthwhile realization supports continued or expanded participation.

claims.text: Meaningful Engagement is downstream behaviour and feedback, not the organizing construct.
Realized Value may influence future participation, but the causal pathway is unvalidated.

nodes.label: Products and transactions
nodes.subtitle: Banking • rewards • partner activity
nodes.definition: The banking products, reward products and transaction infrastructure through which people spend, earn and access benefits.
nodes.roleInSystem: Generates loyalty opportunities, participation routes, qualifying activity and transaction evidence that can influence several value-state transitions.
nodes.whyItMatters: It is an established institutional capability that will be used regardless of how the future loyalty experience is designed.
nodes.known: Bank-linked products can produce additional earning routes and value. Transaction behaviour can reveal where relevant value might exist.
nodes.provisional: Product use does not itself prove loyalty or program engagement, and transaction signals cannot be treated as unrestricted targeting permission.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Clarify which product or transaction conditions create opportunities, establish qualification and provide reliable evidence without treating activity as realized value.

claims.text: Bank-linked products can produce additional earning routes and value. Transaction behaviour can reveal where relevant value might exist.
Product use does not itself prove loyalty or program engagement, and transaction signals cannot be treated as unrestricted targeting permission.

nodes.label: Data and decisioning
nodes.subtitle: Priority connective layer
nodes.definition: The data, identity, analytical and decision processes used to interpret context and determine an appropriate action or opportunity.
nodes.roleInSystem: Helps assess relevance, eligibility, context and performance. Data and decisioning do not create value merely by existing.
nodes.whyItMatters: The core strategic question—what value, to whom, when and through which channel—cannot be answered consistently without usable context and decision governance.
nodes.known: The client has enterprise data and offer-decisioning capabilities. Public evidence does not establish the extent to which they are integrated with the program.
nodes.provisional: More data does not guarantee better decisions. Identity gaps, consent, privacy, bias, incomplete signals and over-targeting can reduce relevance or trust.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Use permitted context to improve relevance and learning while preserving consent, suitability, governance and explainability.

claims.text: The client has enterprise data and offer-decisioning capabilities. Public evidence does not establish the extent to which they are integrated with the program.
More data does not guarantee better decisions. Identity gaps, consent, privacy, bias, incomplete signals and over-targeting can reduce relevance or trust.

nodes.label: Channels and delivery
nodes.subtitle: Program • banking • partner touchpoints
nodes.definition: The digital, physical and communication touchpoints through which decisions, offers, information and experiences reach people.
nodes.roleInSystem: Makes opportunities discoverable and actionable and makes Available accessible for use through appropriate touchpoints.
nodes.whyItMatters: The client already operates mature banking channels, while the program also has standalone surfaces and partner touchpoints.
nodes.known: Multiple channels exist. Separate access, authentication and feature availability have produced some directional signals of discontinuity.
nodes.provisional: Multiple channels are not inherently fragmented. The quality of orchestration, ownership and handoffs across them remains unclear.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Improve opportunity presentation, action access and available-value access without assuming every channel should be integrated.

claims.text: Multiple channels exist. Separate access, authentication and feature availability have produced some directional signals of discontinuity.
Multiple channels are not inherently fragmented. The quality of orchestration, ownership and handoffs across them remains unclear.

nodes.label: Service and operations
nodes.subtitle: Fulfilment • support • recovery
nodes.definition: The operational backbone that calculates and fulfils rewards, supports members, manages issues and coordinates program administration.
nodes.roleInSystem: Supports qualification, posting, release, fulfilment, recovery and especially the movement from Earned to Available.
nodes.whyItMatters: The financial institution already has substantial operating capacity. Reusing relevant capabilities for the program could improve consistency and create economies of scale.
nodes.known: Reliable reward posting, redemption and service recovery influence whether members trust the value proposition. Public signals identify some cross-system support handoffs.
nodes.provisional: The actual degree of integration, duplication or fragmentation between the client and program operating models is unknown.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Improve posting reliability, access, fulfilment and recovery while clarifying ownership across handoffs.

claims.text: Reliable reward posting, redemption and service recovery influence whether members trust the value proposition. Public signals identify some cross-system support handoffs.
The actual degree of integration, duplication or fragmentation between the client and program operating models is unknown.

nodes.label: Interface friction
nodes.subtitle: Partial connectivity • unclear handoffs
nodes.definition: A marker for places where identity, information, value, decisions or service may not move reliably across organizational or technological boundaries.
nodes.roleInSystem: It keeps the map attentive to the quality of interfaces without assuming that every separate system or channel is defective.
nodes.whyItMatters: Separate surfaces, linking issues, delayed rewards and support transfers provide directional evidence that some interfaces may constrain value delivery.
nodes.known: Specific member-facing breakdowns have been reported. The existence of multiple channels and systems is also supported.
nodes.provisional: Those signals do not establish enterprise-wide fragmentation or prove that tighter integration will always create net gains.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Identify which interfaces require better coordination and which separations are intentional, protective or economically sensible.

claims.text: Specific member-facing breakdowns have been reported. The existence of multiple channels and systems is also supported.
Those signals do not establish enterprise-wide fragmentation or prove that tighter integration will always create net gains.

nodes.label: Permissioned identity and data
nodes.subtitle: Connected context under governance
nodes.definition: A governed ability to recognize the same person or relationship across program, banking and partner contexts where permitted.
nodes.roleInSystem: It would create the usable context required for decisioning without treating ownership as unrestricted access to all member data.
nodes.whyItMatters: Relevant orchestration depends on knowing which signals belong together and which uses the person has consented to.
nodes.known: Program and banking relationships generate different data. Privacy, consent and organizational access conditions apply to any connection.
nodes.provisional: The current identity architecture, consent model, data rights and cross-organizational access are not established. Constrained by TB2 Trust and consent. Joann, Lia and Josh each modelled permission as something intrusion spends rather than a resource the system holds. Personalization intensity raises perceived intrusion, which narrows consent, which thins the very signal this capability depends on. This capability is therefore a consequence of being trusted, not a precondition that can simply be built.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Connect only the context required to create explainable member and partner value under clear governance.

claims.text: Program and banking relationships generate different data. Privacy, consent and organizational access conditions apply to any connection.
The current identity architecture, consent model, data rights and cross-organizational access are not established.
This capability is a future hypothesis, not a committed solution architecture.

nodes.label: Integrated value orchestration
nodes.subtitle: What value • to whom • when • where
nodes.definition: A proposed capability for selecting and coordinating the most relevant available value for a particular relationship and moment.
nodes.roleInSystem: Coordinates which opportunities or value pathways may be relevant to whom, when, where and for what intended member outcome.
nodes.whyItMatters: The system contains many products, partners and channels. Without orchestration, additional options can increase complexity rather than realized value.
nodes.known: The client has broader offer-decisioning capabilities and has publicly emphasized personalization. Member-recognized program personalization is not yet established.
nodes.provisional: Decision relevance, operating ownership, model governance and the incremental effect on engagement remain hypotheses.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Test solution-neutral mechanisms for improving relevant paths toward realized outcomes; personalization remains a possible lever rather than the outcome.

claims.text: The client has broader offer-decisioning capabilities and has publicly emphasized personalization. Member-recognized program personalization is not yet established.
Decision relevance, operating ownership, model governance and the incremental effect on engagement remain hypotheses.
This capability is a future hypothesis, not a committed solution architecture.

nodes.label: Coordinated delivery
nodes.subtitle: Channels • fulfilment • service recovery
nodes.definition: A future state in which relevant decisions move coherently through channels, fulfilment and service recovery.
nodes.roleInSystem: Carries selected opportunities and value coherently through channels, fulfilment, access and recovery.
nodes.whyItMatters: Relevant targeting cannot produce meaningful engagement if access, posting, redemption or issue resolution fails.
nodes.known: Channels and service capabilities already exist, while some public signals show reliability and handoff issues.
nodes.provisional: The degree of coordination required, implementation cost and risk of tightly coupled failures remain unknown. Constrained by TB3 Value gap. Henry and Sly drew this as a closed loop rather than a capability: promised value that does not visibly arrive creates uncertainty, which triggers detection and resolution effort, which restores clarity. Coordinated delivery only holds if that correction loop is working; installing the capability does not by itself close the gap.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Test whether fit-for-purpose coordination improves access and reliable fulfilment without creating tightly coupled failure modes.

claims.text: Channels and service capabilities already exist, while some public signals show reliability and handoff issues.
The degree of coordination required, implementation cost and risk of tightly coupled failures remain unknown.
This capability is a future hypothesis, not a committed solution architecture.

nodes.label: Member-Client Intersection
nodes.subtitle: Relationship structure • not proof of value
nodes.definition: A larger and more engaged population holding both program and banking relationships.
nodes.roleInSystem: Represents people holding both program and banking relationships. Movement into or depth within the intersection is a possible downstream outcome, not the purpose of the system.
nodes.whyItMatters: The client explicitly intends to convert relevant non-client members and deepen relationships with existing clients.
nodes.known: The intersection can grow through two different pathways: member-to-client conversion and client-to-member enrolment.
nodes.provisional: More linked relationships do not automatically create affinity, retention, incremental revenue or realized member value.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Evaluate appropriate, need-led relationship progression only where demonstrable incremental member value exists.

claims.text: The intersection can grow through two different pathways: member-to-client conversion and client-to-member enrolment.
More linked relationships do not automatically create affinity, retention, incremental revenue or realized member value.

nodes.label: Sustainable net relationship value
nodes.subtitle: Consumer + business economics
nodes.definition: The incremental economic and strategic value created across consumer and business relationships after the full cost of the program is considered.
nodes.roleInSystem: It is the client’s ultimate organizational outcome and prevents revenue growth from being assessed without the costs and liabilities required to produce it.
nodes.whyItMatters: Engagement, membership and higher spending are not sufficient evidence of ROI unless they are incremental and exceed rewards, technology, operating and risk costs.
nodes.known: Potential benefits include acquisition, product use, share of wallet, retention, partner revenue, insight and economies of scale.
nodes.provisional: Incrementality, partner economics, conversion persistence, total costs and the time required to realize returns remain unmeasured. Constrained by TB1 Program economics. Joann, Ola and Josh independently found the brake that sits under this outcome: realization up, redemption up, breakage revenue down, margin headroom down, offer generosity down. This outcome is reachable only if breakage is replaced as the measure, which is what the conversion pathway below is for.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Build a measurement model that connects engagement and relationship movement to causal, long-term net value.

claims.text: Potential benefits include acquisition, product use, share of wallet, retention, partner revenue, insight and economies of scale.
Incrementality, partner economics, conversion persistence, total costs and the time required to realize returns remain unmeasured.

nodes.label: Non-member / non-client
nodes.subtitle: No current program or banking relationship
nodes.definition: People who are not currently loyalty-program members or banking clients of the institution.
nodes.roleInSystem: They sit outside the active relationship system because the current inquiry focuses on engagement and movement among people who already hold at least one relationship.
nodes.whyItMatters: Their eventual entry matters for growth, but modelling acquisition tactics in detail would expand the inquiry beyond the activation and relationship system currently being examined.
nodes.known: A person could enter the boundary by joining the program, becoming a banking client, or establishing both relationships.
nodes.provisional: The size, needs, awareness and likelihood of entry for this population have not been established by the current research.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Treat boundary entry as a downstream consequence of the system’s reputation and value—not as the primary behaviour the present map must explain.

systemLinks.explanation: These are the two primary entry states if a person establishes one relationship.
These outcomes may strengthen reputation and create entry reasons, but the connection remains indirect and is not drawn as an internal flow.

claims.text: A person could enter the boundary by joining the program, becoming a banking client, or establishing both relationships.
The size, needs, awareness and likelihood of entry for this population have not been established by the current research.

nodes.label: Customer expectations and market norms
nodes.subtitle: Personalization • simplicity • flexibility • trust
nodes.definition: Changing expectations about relevance, personalization, ease of use, flexibility, transparency and dependable service.
nodes.roleInSystem: This influence shapes the standard against which people judge program, banking and partner value without being controlled by the bounded system.
nodes.whyItMatters: The client’s problem statement explicitly links the need for deeper relationships to changing customer needs, while primary research emphasizes flexibility, relevance and reliable value delivery.
nodes.known: Members compare loyalty value against alternative programs, cash equivalents, service expectations and the effort required to use benefits.
nodes.provisional: The relative importance of each expectation varies by population, context and moment; the map does not assume one universal preference profile.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Use expectations as a design and validation condition rather than treating personalization or engagement as inherently valuable.

systemLinks.explanation: Expectations shape whether available value feels understandable, accessible and worth continued participation.
Future capabilities would need to meet evolving expectations without over-personalizing or increasing complexity.

claims.text: Members compare loyalty value against alternative programs, cash equivalents, service expectations and the effort required to use benefits.
The relative importance of each expectation varies by population, context and moment; the map does not assume one universal preference profile.

nodes.label: Technology landscape
nodes.subtitle: AI • identity • open-data capabilities
nodes.definition: The changing availability and maturity of technologies that can support prediction, personalization, identity resolution, data portability and coordinated delivery.
nodes.roleInSystem: It changes what may be technically possible, expected or economically feasible, but it does not determine which capabilities should be adopted.
nodes.whyItMatters: Artificial intelligence and data portability may expand decisioning options while also creating new governance, trust and operating requirements.
nodes.known: The institution has broader enterprise data and AI ambitions. Program-specific integration and demonstrated member value remain unconfirmed.
nodes.provisional: Technology maturity, implementation cost, model quality, interoperability and incremental impact on engagement are unresolved.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Evaluate technology only where it improves a defined value or operating flow under appropriate governance.

systemLinks.explanation: External technology options may improve or complicate how signals, decisions and fulfilment move across existing capabilities.
These hypothesized capabilities depend partly on available technology, but technology alone does not establish their value or feasibility.

claims.text: The institution has broader enterprise data and AI ambitions. Program-specific integration and demonstrated member value remain unconfirmed.
Technology maturity, implementation cost, model quality, interoperability and incremental impact on engagement are unresolved.

nodes.label: Regulation, privacy and consent environment
nodes.subtitle: Permitted use • accountability • protection
nodes.definition: The laws, regulatory expectations, privacy rules and consent conditions governing the collection, connection, use and exchange of data and value.
nodes.roleInSystem: This environment defines permissible operating conditions for identity, decisioning, marketing, partner insight and cross-system data use.
nodes.whyItMatters: Ownership of a program does not imply unrestricted access to or use of member information; permission and purpose remain necessary conditions.
nodes.known: Privacy, consent, suitability and governance requirements apply to any connection between program, banking and partner contexts.
nodes.provisional: The specific legal interpretation, data rights, consent architecture and partner-sharing limits are outside the present research scope.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Treat governance as a design input from the outset rather than a downstream compliance check.

systemLinks.explanation: Regulatory and consent conditions affect which signals may be used, which actions are suitable and what information may flow to partners.
Governance defines the operating envelope for the future pathway and may intentionally preserve separation between some systems.

claims.text: Privacy, consent, suitability and governance requirements apply to any connection between program, banking and partner contexts.
The specific legal interpretation, data rights, consent architecture and partner-sharing limits are outside the present research scope.

nodes.label: Competitor loyalty and financial ecosystems
nodes.subtitle: Alternative programs • products • value propositions
nodes.definition: Other loyalty, banking, card and partner ecosystems against which people and businesses compare the client’s value proposition.
nodes.roleInSystem: Competitors provide alternative relationships, benefits and participation options without being actors inside the bounded client-program system.
nodes.whyItMatters: Primary research shows that members compare reward economics, flexibility, perks and service across multiple programs rather than evaluating one program in isolation.
nodes.known: Alternative reward products and ecosystems affect members’ reference points and can compete for spending, attention and partner participation.
nodes.provisional: Competitor-specific performance, switching behaviour and direct effects on this program have not been measured in the current analysis.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Use competitor ecosystems as contextual benchmarks while preserving a member-value definition grounded in actual needs rather than feature imitation.

systemLinks.explanation: Alternative programs affect value comparisons, participation choices and the attractiveness of the partner network.
Competitive responses may influence whether improved engagement persists and produces incremental organizational value.

claims.text: Alternative reward products and ecosystems affect members’ reference points and can compete for spending, attention and partner participation.
Competitor-specific performance, switching behaviour and direct effects on this program have not been measured in the current analysis.

nodes.subtitle: Posted points a member already holds
nodes.definition: The stock of posted points a member holds. It fills two ways. Most of it is earned through qualifying activity and posts once processed. The rest arrives at enrolment: signing up grants roughly 750 points, which is still earned — enrolment is the qualifying behaviour — it simply completes in one step.
nodes.roleInSystem: Sits between Earned and Available. It is why the progression is sequential without being one mandatory journey: a member joins the cycle at whichever state their balance already puts them in. A brand-new member is already holding available value, and a five-year customer holds a balance regardless of this week's activity.
nodes.whyItMatters: Raised on 12 September: 'you're assuming they're starting from zero — you can have available value even if you haven't earned points on a specific offer.' Without this the diagram implies every member starts at the catalogue, which almost none do. The sign-up grant is the clearest case: the offer is weighed by a prospect, enrolment earns it, and it posts immediately.
nodes.known: Sign-up grants roughly 750 points, earned by enrolling.
nodes.provisional: The actual sign-up grant, expiry behaviour and how balance is segmented by member type are not yet established.
nodes.opportunityImplication: A member's entry state is a design input for onboarding and for the ledger.
chain: Member enters at whichever state their balance allows

nodes.subtitle: Owns the liability
nodes.definition: The function that owns the outstanding points liability and the programme's margin. It decides how much the programme can afford to give away, and it is scored on breakage - the value members never collect.
nodes.roleInSystem: Sets the economic ceiling the rest of the system operates under. Offer generosity, point value and how much can be funded are decided here, not in the product.
nodes.whyItMatters: It appears in the stakeholder grid as keep satisfied - high power, low interest - and it owns the only constraint the team identified as arithmetic rather than behavioural. The highest-leverage intervention in the analysis has to be agreed by the stakeholder the team engages with least.
nodes.known: Holds the outstanding points liability and is measured on breakage.
nodes.provisional: How generosity decisions are actually made, and what would have to replace breakage as a measure, are not established.
nodes.opportunityImplication: Realized value is the candidate replacement measure, which is what the ledger would produce.

nodes.subtitle: Sets the goal and the priorities
nodes.definition: The client team and its executive sponsors - the people who decide what the programme is for, what gets built, and what the organisation is measured on.
nodes.roleInSystem: Sets the system goal and allocates the capacity that delivers it.
nodes.whyItMatters: Changing what the system optimises for is the highest-leverage intervention four contributors identified, and it is decided here. The product can supply the evidence; it cannot make the decision.
nodes.known: Sits in manage closely - high power, high interest.
nodes.provisional: Where goal-setting authority actually sits between the client team, sponsors and the wider business is not established.
nodes.opportunityImplication: This is the audience for the realized-value argument.

valueStates.label: Opportunity
valueStates.definition: Every reward, benefit, offer and earning possibility the programme makes available — the whole catalogue, before any member filter is applied. It is programme-level, not member-level: an opportunity exists whether or not any particular member ever sees it. Nothing here is anyone's.
valueStates.entryCondition: A partner, product or programme proposition exists and is live.
valueStates.exitCondition: The system surfaces it to a particular member as relevant and eligible.
valueStates.plainLanguage: Every reward the programme offers. Not yet pointed at anyone — and whoever eventually sees it may be a prospect, not a member.

valueStates.label: Potential
valueStates.definition: The rewards that reached a particular member, and which that member is weighing up. Two things have happened: the catalogue was filtered to them, and they are working out what it is worth to them — is it attainable, is it worth the effort, is it what they actually want. It is called potential value because this is where value first exists in the member's eyes, as something they could have. Nothing is theirs yet. At the very front of the chain the person weighing it may not be a member yet: a join-and-get-750-points offer is weighed by a prospect, who becomes a member by acting on it.
valueStates.entryCondition: The opportunity is surfaced to this member as relevant and eligible, and the member begins weighing it.
valueStates.exitCondition: The member decides to act and completes the qualifying requirement.
valueStates.plainLanguage: The rewards that reached this person, and they're working out whether it's worth it. At the very front of the chain that person may still be a prospect.

valueStates.label: Earned
valueStates.definition: Value the member has decided to act on and acted to secure — they completed the qualifying purchase, activity or requirement. The decision has been made and carried out, but the value may not have posted yet. Enrolment counts: signing up is itself a qualifying behaviour, which is how a sign-up grant of roughly 750 points is earned rather than simply appearing.
valueStates.entryCondition: The member acts on the opportunity and satisfies the applicable qualification rule.
valueStates.exitCondition: The earned value posts into the member's balance and becomes usable.
valueStates.plainLanguage: The member did the thing — including, at the very start, signing up. It's theirs, even if it hasn't landed yet.

valueStates.label: Available
valueStates.definition: Earned value that has been posted, released, activated or otherwise made accessible for use.
valueStates.entryCondition: The member can operationally access or use the earned entitlement.
valueStates.exitCondition: The member successfully uses or converts the value.
valueStates.plainLanguage: It's posted into the balance and ready to spend.

valueStates.label: Realized
valueStates.definition: Value the member has successfully used or converted into a worthwhile outcome that the system can measure. Reworded on 12 September to make the outcome measurable rather than only perceived, so the product can show a member that their value has been measured.
valueStates.entryCondition: Successful use or conversion produces a recognized outcome.
valueStates.exitCondition: The value episode is evaluated and may influence subsequent participation.
valueStates.plainLanguage: The member used it, and we can show what it was worth.

valueTransitions.definition: The catalogue is filtered and surfaced to a particular member, who begins assessing what the reward is worth to them.
entryConditions: Relevance and a plausible eligible path are established for a particular member and context.
exitConditions: The next controlled state is reached.

valueTransitions.name: Used and converted into something worthwhile

valueTransitions.definition: The outcome is perceived as sufficiently worthwhile and trustworthy to influence future behaviour.
entryConditions: The outcome is perceived as sufficiently worthwhile and trustworthy to influence future behaviour.
exitConditions: A future participation response is observed.
valueTransitions.frictionOrDelay: To be specified from evidence for each population and pathway.
openQuestions: Treat as inferred until behaviour-over-time evidence validates it.
valueTransitions.name: Shapes what the member does next

relationships.label: Optional banking adoption
relationships.relationshipDefinition: A Member-Only participant may enter the intersection when a relevant need leads to suitable banking adoption.

relationships.label: Program enrolment
relationships.relationshipDefinition: A Client-Only participant enters the intersection structurally through enrolment, but status does not prove realized value.

relationships.label: Standalone realization pathway
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Member-Only participants must be able to realize credible standalone program and partner value.

relationships.label: Combined realization pathway
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Combined relationships may create additional routes to value, but linked status does not prove incremental value.

relationships.label: Enrolment → first realized value
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Relevant enrolment creates a possible path toward the first realized program outcome.

relationships.label: Opportunities + fulfilment
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Partners contribute propositions, access, experiences and fulfilment that can support value realization.

relationships.label: Participation + partner returns
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Member participation may create sales, affinity, insight or reach, but incrementality is unresolved.

relationships.label: Qualification + transaction evidence
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Product activity can create qualification and transaction evidence where use is permitted.

relationships.label: Opportunities + earning conditions
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Products and transactions generate opportunities, participation routes and earning conditions.

relationships.label: Relevance + eligibility context
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Decisioning may help assess relevance and eligibility without itself creating value.

relationships.label: Presentation + access
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Channels present opportunities and provide action or available-value access.

relationships.label: Posting + fulfilment + recovery
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Operations support posting, release, fulfilment and recovery.

relationships.label: Continued / expanded participation
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Worthwhile realized outcomes may influence sustained participation; the causal effect is unvalidated.

relationships.label: Value realization + participation signals
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Observed outcomes and participation provide signals for measurement and future decisions.

relationships.label: Identity + permission handoffs
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Identity or permission handoffs may interrupt usable context.

relationships.label: Channel continuity constraints
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Separate surfaces may create repeated steps or inconsistent context.

relationships.label: Support + fulfilment ownership
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Cross-system issues may be transferred rather than resolved end to end.

relationships.label: Reaches the member, who weighs it
relationships.displayLabel: Reaches the member, who weighs it
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Two changes at once. The catalogue narrows to one person — decisioning selects what is relevant and eligible, a channel surfaces it. And the member starts assessing it: whether it is attainable, worth the effort, and what they actually want. Value first exists in the member's eyes at this point, as something they could have.

relationships.label: Member decides to act, and acts
relationships.displayLabel: Member decides to act, and acts
relationships.relationshipDefinition: The member commits: they make the qualifying purchase or complete the required activity. This is the step where value becomes theirs.

relationships.label: Post + release + activate
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Earned becomes Available when the entitlement is operationally accessible.

relationships.label: Use + convert into worthwhile outcome
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Available becomes Realized through successful use or conversion into perceived worth.

relationships.label: Propositions + benefits
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Partner contributions create sources of opportunity.

relationships.label: Products + participation routes
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Products and transactions create opportunity and earning routes.

relationships.label: Relevance and eligibility
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Decisioning determines which of the catalogue's rewards reach this member as relevant and eligible — and therefore what the member has to weigh up at all.

relationships.label: Posting + release reliability
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Operations influence whether earned entitlements become accessible.

relationships.label: Access + use pathway
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Channels influence whether available value can be discovered and used.

relationships.label: Fulfilment + recovery
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Fulfilment and recovery influence successful value use.

relationships.label: Qualification + posting stalls
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Interface friction may stall qualification, posting or release.

relationships.label: Governed permitted context
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Permissioned identity may provide usable context under governance.

relationships.label: Coordinated value-path decision
relationships.relationshipDefinition: A selected value pathway may be carried into delivery and operations.

relationships.label: Access + reliable fulfilment
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Coordinated delivery may improve access, fulfilment and recovery.

relationships.label: Partner matching + insight
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Partners may be matched to relevant needs and receive performance learning.

relationships.label: Appropriate relationship progression
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Sustained participation may support appropriate progression; causality is unresolved.

relationships.label: Relationship economics after full costs
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Relationship structure may contribute to net value only after incrementality, liabilities and costs.

relationships.label: Distinct partner + organizational returns
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Partner returns may contribute to organizational value but remain distinct from member outcomes.

relationships.label: Relevant opportunities + fulfilment
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Future partner participation may support relevant opportunities and fulfilment.

relationships.label: Governance context
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Regulation, privacy and consent conditions shape which emerging technologies and uses are permissible.

relationships.label: Capability signals
relationships.relationshipDefinition: New technological possibilities can raise expectations for relevance, immediacy, portability and ease of use.

relationships.label: Market reference points
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Competing ecosystems influence the standards people use to compare value, flexibility, service and access.

relationships.label: Alternative value propositions
relationships.relationshipDefinition: People outside the boundary can choose alternative loyalty and financial relationships before entering this system.

relationships.label: Entry expectations
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Expectations about value, trust and effort shape the threshold for establishing a first relationship.

relationships.label: Partner earn and redeem surface
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Partner brands supply the merchant surfaces, categories and offers through which points are earned and redeemed. Without partner coverage there is less for products and transactions to carry.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Decisions reach the member
relationships.relationshipDefinition: A decision about relevance, eligibility or timing only affects a member once it is delivered through a channel. Decisioning quality is capped by what delivery can carry.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Operational outcomes return as evidence
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Fulfilment results, exceptions and unresolved cases return to decisioning as evidence about what actually completed, not merely what was offered.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Operational support of delivery
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Service and operations sustain the channels members transact through, including recovery when a channel interaction fails.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Members act through delivery channels
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Member-only participants encounter the programme through delivery channels, not solely as a source of value realization.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Member-clients transact through products
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Members who also bank with BMO interact with the products and transactions backbone directly, which is what makes combined signal possible.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Clients hold and transact through products
relationships.displayLabel: Clients hold and transact through products
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Client-only participants interact with the products backbone even where they do not participate in the loyalty programme.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Engagement returns to realization
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Sustained engagement produces further opportunities to realize value, closing the pair rather than terminating at the outcome.
relationships.provenance: Added 10 Sept 2026 in response to faculty feedback that the appendix systems map read as one-way flow into a single outcome. Proposed by Josh, actioned by Joann.

relationships.label: Reinvested relationship value
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Net relationship value returns to fund the value members can realize, closing the pathway instead of terminating at an outcome. This is the only revenue source in the team's analysis that grows when redemption grows, which is why it is the candidate replacement for breakage.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026. Closes the conversion pathway that Joann and Josh both drew as a loop (TR2) but which this view left open.

relationships.label: Where the member sees it
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Sly, 12 September: 'if you see an opportunity, where are you seeing it? You're seeing it within a channel.' An opportunity that no channel carries does not reach anyone.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 from Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change, not one each.

relationships.label: Help understanding it
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Sly, 12 September: 'if you see an opportunity, you don't really understand, and you need more information - service and operations can help you understand it.'
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 from Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change, not one each.

relationships.label: What gets surfaced at all
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Sly, 12 September: 'maybe there's some data behind the scenes that is actually showing that opportunity to you.' Decisioning determines which propositions become visible opportunities.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 from Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change, not one each.

relationships.label: Enter at any stage
relationships.relationshipDefinition: A standing balance places the member directly at available value without passing through opportunity, potential or earned value for that balance. The sequence between states still holds; the member's entry point into it does not have to be the start.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 from Josh's challenge that members do not start from zero.

relationships.label: Posts into the balance
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Earned value accumulates into the member's standing balance once it posts. Points that are earned but not yet posted sit outside the balance, which is the gap a member experiences as pending.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026. The balance sits between earned and available value, not beside them.

relationships.label: Where they weigh it
relationships.relationshipDefinition: The member compares, reads the terms and works out what it is worth inside a channel. A reward the channel presents badly is weighed badly, whatever the offer itself is.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026, completing Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change.

relationships.label: Where the action is taken
relationships.relationshipDefinition: The qualifying action usually runs through a channel: activating an offer, linking a card, completing the purchase on a surface the programme can see. A channel that does not register the action means the member acted and the system did not notice.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026, completing Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change.

relationships.label: Where the balance is seen
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Value being posted and the member knowing it was posted are two different things. A channel is what turns available value into value the member is aware they hold.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026, completing Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change.

relationships.label: Answers can I get this
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Eligibility questions, terms and qualification rules are what a member needs resolved before they can decide. Service is what answers them, and unanswered questions stall the assessment.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026, completing Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change.

relationships.label: Decides the action counted
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Qualification processing determines whether what the member did actually satisfies the rule. This is where a member who believes they earned something and a system that disagrees part company.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026, completing Sylvester's challenge that the enabling capabilities touch every state change.

relationships.label: Funds what can be offered
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Margin headroom decides how generous an offer can be and what a point is worth. The product does not set this.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 with the governance actors, from the stakeholder grid.

relationships.label: Realized value reduces breakage
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Value members actually collect is value the programme no longer keeps. This is the inverse link behind the breakage brake, and it is arithmetic: a point that gets used cannot also go unused.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 with the governance actors, from the stakeholder grid.

relationships.label: Sets what the system optimises for
relationships.displayLabel: Sets what the system optimises for
relationships.relationshipDefinition: The organising goal - whether the system is scored on value issued, activity, breakage or realized value - is decided here.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 with the governance actors, from the stakeholder grid.

relationships.label: Sets decision priorities
relationships.relationshipDefinition: What decisioning is pointed at, and what counts as a good decision, follows from what leadership asks to be measured.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 with the governance actors, from the stakeholder grid.

relationships.label: Allocates operating capacity
relationships.relationshipDefinition: How much capacity exists for posting, fulfilment and recovery is a funding decision, not an operational one.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 with the governance actors, from the stakeholder grid.

relationships.label: Reports the economics
relationships.relationshipDefinition: Liability, margin and breakage are what leadership sees when deciding what the programme can do.
relationships.provenance: Added 12 Sept 2026 with the governance actors, from the stakeholder grid.

overlays.statement: Recognize and understand an opportunity that is relevant and worthwhile.
Improve identification, relevance, reach and understandability of worthwhile opportunities.
Complete the required activity with reasonable preparation, effort and confidence.
Reduce effort, preparation, complexity and failure in earning value.
Know whether value was earned, what it is worth and when it can be used.
Improve legibility, trust, posting reliability, accessibility and recovery for earned value.
Use available value in a meaningful moment, channel or context with acceptable effort.
Convert more available value into worthwhile outcomes through usability, contextual reach, flexibility and successful fulfilment.
Decide whether to return, broaden, continue or discontinue participation.
Reinforce continued participation through consistently worthwhile outcomes and learning.
Convert more earned loyalty value into realized member value by reducing barriers to understanding, accessing and using it in meaningful moments and contexts.

views.label: 1. Current System
views.heading: Current System
views.purpose: Show what exists today and where value progression may be enabled, interrupted, delayed or obscured.
views.contextParagraph: This view shows the populations, partners, value flows and institutional capabilities operating today. It highlights where loyalty value may progress or stall between Opportunity, Potential, Earned, Available and Realized, while preserving uncertainty about the actual degree of integration, fragmentation and causal effect.
exclusions: Future capabilities are not operational current-state components.
interpretationRules: Structural arrows do not establish causal effects.

views.label: 2. How Value Progresses
views.heading: How value progresses
views.purpose: Show the stages worthwhile value passes through on its way to the member, and where that progression may stall. This is a stage view, not a second systems map: value moves forward through the states and does not return to an earlier one.
views.contextParagraph: This view uses Realized value as the system main variable. It shows how loyalty opportunities progress from Opportunity to Potential, Earned, Available and ultimately Realized; where that progression may stall; and which system conditions, member needs and broad opportunity areas could improve the amount, relevance, reliability, accessibility, usefulness and appropriate speed of realized value.
exclusions: JTBDs and DVOs are overlays, not operating components.
interpretationRules: VT05 is feedback after the canonical value-state chain.

viewNote.title: What it's for
paragraphs: It's a diagnostic tool for locating loss. “Members don't get value” is unactionable. Splitting it into five steps lets you ask which step — and each step has a different owner and a different fix. Posting failing is an operations problem. Use and conversion failing is a discovery and channel problem. Without the split you'd treat them as one thing and fix the wrong one.
This is a value progression, not a systems map. It shows the language we use at each stage, not the structure of the system — that is view 1.

Read it in three bands. The top row is the five states value passes through — it starts programme-wide as the whole catalogue, narrows to one member, then becomes theirs. The middle row is what moves it between them, and each of those touches several stages rather than one: a member sees an opportunity in a channel, service explains it, data decides what gets surfaced at all. The bottom row is what stalls value, and where members actually join.

The sequence holds — value cannot reach available without being earned — but a member can join at any point. Signing up grants roughly 750 points, so a new member holds a balance having earned nothing.

Note who is actually in each state. The last three belong to a member. The first two need not: a join-and-get-750-points offer is weighed by a prospect, who becomes a member by acting on it. Enrolment is itself a qualifying behaviour, which is why a sign-up grant is earned rather than simply appearing — it just completes in one step and posts immediately.

views.label: 7. Future Opportunity
views.heading: Future Opportunity
views.purpose: Show a hypothesized improved system if relevant value-state transitions are strengthened.
views.contextParagraph: This view shows a hypothesized improved system in which governed context, coordinated decisions, delivery, fulfilment and recovery could help more loyalty value become relevant, earned, available and ultimately realized. The capabilities and downstream outcomes remain opportunity hypotheses rather than a committed solution architecture or proven causal model.
exclusions: No capability is a committed target architecture.
interpretationRules: Member, partner and organizational outcomes remain distinct.

views.label: 3. Outside the Boundary
views.heading: Outside the System Boundary
views.purpose: Show external actors and conditions without treating them as internal components.
views.contextParagraph: This view isolates external actors and conditions that may influence the bounded system. Only relationships among external factors are drawn; possible links to current and future nodes remain narrative and contextual rather than established internal flows.
interpretationRules: External factors influence but are not controlled by the bounded system.

materialAssumptions: Current transition rates and realization gaps are unknown.
Causal effects from realization to engagement and relationship outcomes are unvalidated.
The current degree of integration or fragmentation is unresolved.
Partner incrementality and sustainable net value after full costs remain unresolved.

flowLenses.purpose: A systems map that offers only one kind of arrow can only read as a pipeline. Reading the same structure through separate flow lenses is what makes the interconnections visible.
flowLenses.method: Adopted from Joann's MMIE 884 Assignment 3, which reads its map through matter, money and information flows.

lenses.label: Value flow
lenses.definition: The reward value itself moving toward the member — opportunity, fulfilment, benefit.

lenses.label: Information flow
lenses.definition: Signal, evidence, status and decisioning moving through the system.

lenses.label: Participation flow
lenses.definition: People entering the system, acting in it, and returning to it.

lenses.label: Structural condition
lenses.definition: Friction obstructing rather than carrying — the negative links in the view.

terminology.rule: One term per concept. Where the team used several words for the same thing, the agreed term is the one listed as 'use'.

entries.note: Agreed on the call: 'we were all using different words for the same point... moving forward I'd recommend us just sticking to one.' This is the starting point for the data dictionary.

entries.plainLanguage: Transaction data - how much the system is permitted to know about a member.
entries.note: Flagged on the call as jargon needing a layman's translation.

openCollision.resolution: Realized value is the main variable — the amount of worthwhile value members actually obtain. The five stages drop the word entirely and read Opportunity, Potential, Earned, Available, Realized, because the band is already labelled as value states and repeating it on each one is what caused the collision.

stakeholderBinding.note: Which stakeholders hold power over each part of the system. The grid answers who can move the system; this binds that answer to the components they can move. Assignment is analytical judgement, not an org chart.
stakeholderBinding.sharpEdge: Finance and Risk sit in keep satisfied - high power, low interest - and they own the points liability, which makes them the owners of the breakage brake. The team's highest-leverage intervention has to be agreed by the quadrant the team talks to least.
